summary: Four studies directly apply graph neural networks (message passing over relational graphs) to fraud detection, and one additional study applies a non-GNN method to the same task for comparison. [V0049] (Chen et al., 2020) applies message passing over relational graphs to identifying fraudulent transactions on the LedgerGuard dataset, achieving 0.94 accuracy — the strongest reported result among GNN-based fraud detection studies in this set. [V0052] (Fischer et al., 2023) applies the same GNN paradigm to fraudulent transaction identification on the GridWatch dataset, reporting an F1 score of 0.80. [V0051] (El-Sayed et al., 2022) also uses message passing over relational graphs for fraud detection, evaluated on ToxiBench, with an AUROC of 0.73. [V0050] (Duarte et al., 2021) applies message passing over relational graphs to fraudulent transaction identification on CellLife, reporting MAE of 0.66 — a regression-style metric suggesting a different evaluation framing. As a non-GNN baseline on the same fraud detection task, [V0064] (Adebayo et al., 2026) uses boosted decision-tree ensembles on GridWatch, achieving 0.78 AUROC, which is lower than the GNN F1 reported by [V0052] on the same dataset (though metrics differ). Documents applying GNNs to other tasks (e.g., agricultural yield [V0027], hate speech [V0097]) or applying non-GNN methods to fraud detection [V0072] are excluded from the top five as they do not satisfy both criteria simultaneously.
